tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).

- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

 ## D15. Company-site crawl limit is per run
 
 - `--max-pages` (default 60) sets how many top-ranked company-site URLs are fetched. Campfire is collected with `--max-pages 120`: its leaders appear mostly in blog bylines, and the default left 35 posts unfetched. With 120 it fetched 86 pages and hit no cap. Robinhood keeps 60: more newsroom pages there mostly add stale appointment posts and LLM cost.
+
+## D16. Currency and confidence rules (Phase 3; proxy and 18-month rules decided by Daniel)
+
+All deterministic, in `pipeline/resolve.py`. The LLM only reports what a page says (`status`: current / former / incoming / unclear).
+- **One role per (seniority, function) per person.** The best claim names it: source priority (company_site > sec_filing > search), then newest date.
+- **Former wins** unless a current claim for that role is strictly newer (undated counts as oldest). A "former" next to the title in the snippet overrides the model's status. Test: Jason Warnick ("former Chief Financial Officer" in the 2026 proxy) is never current, with or without the 2021 newsroom post.
+- **Proxy rule:** for C-level roles, a **dated** newsroom or search claim older than the latest DEF 14A, for a role the proxy doesn't list for that person, is `is_current = false`. SEC claims are exempt. **Undated** claims (e.g. the investors.robinhood.com leadership page) can't be shown to be older: they stay current and are listed in `c_level_not_in_proxy_undated`. The proxy lists only Section 16 officers, so a Chief People Officer or CISO is normally absent from it. (The first run applied the rule to undated claims too and wrongly retired 7 people. Fixed and tested.)
+- **Promotion rule:** an older title is superseded by a later dated title in the same function (Gretchen Howard: VP of Operations in 2018, then COO in 2019). Founder roles are never superseded.
+- **Confidence per role:** `high` = an SEC filing, or 2+ sources including the company site. `medium` = the company site, or 2+ sources. `low` = a single search result. **An uncorroborated single-source role last dated more than 18 months ago is `low`** and listed (`stale_single_source`). A person's confidence is that of their best current role.
+- **Listed for review, not decided:** two current holders of the same C-level seat (`seat_conflicts`, e.g. Campfire's two CTOs); sources that disagree on currency (`conflicts`); different locations; nickname merges; possible duplicates; records from bot-blocked hosts (D13).
+- People with no current role are kept (with their facts), so "who was the CFO before?" can be answered. Lists and counts include only current roles.
+- **Rejected:** letting the LLM decide currency or confidence. It doesn't know other sources or the proxy date, and its answer isn't auditable.
+
+## D17. Extraction: structured outputs, cached, pre-filtered
+
+- **Chosen:** `messages.parse(output_format=Extraction)` (Pydantic, `effort=medium`), one call per pre-filtered document, 4 in parallel.
+- **Rejected:** tool use with a forced tool choice. `claude-sonnet-5-5` rejects forced `tool_choice` (HTTP 400). Structured outputs guarantee the schema without a fake tool. The spec's "tool use + Pydantic" intent (schema-validated output) is unchanged.
+- **Pre-filter:** keep ±3 lines around role words (chief, officer, VP, head of, founder, ...) plus date lines. For SEC filings, use the executive-officers section, else the signatures. Pages with no role word skip the LLM. About 12% of documents are skipped.
+- **Context:** the prompt names the target company and domain, and asks for the employer plus a `works_at_target_company` flag. That flag rejects customers, partners, and homonymous organizations (campfire.org, robinhood.org).
+- **Cache:** responses are cached at `data/<domain>/raw/_extractions/` (gitignored with the rest of the raw data), keyed by model, prompt version, URL and exact input. Re-resolving costs $0. `--reextract` forces new calls. `stats_json` reports both this run's cost and the cost of the cached responses.
+- **Refusals / truncation:** a response without structured output is recorded in `extraction_errors` and that document is skipped. No server-side fallback model: a refusal is unlikely on public leadership text, and a silent model switch would muddy cost and provenance.
+
+## D18. Evidence check, with literal re-anchoring
+
+- A claim is kept only if all of these hold: the name appears in the cached source text; the snippet appears literally in it (whitespace, curly quotes and dashes don't count); the snippet contains the last name and the exact title; the title passes the title rules (`titles.py`); the model says the role is held at the target company; and the name has at least two tokens.
+- **Re-anchoring:** the model often takes the title from a heading but quotes a sentence that rewords it ("Vice President, Corporate Finance & Investor Relations" vs "Vice President of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations"). When the exact name and exact title are both in the source within 200 characters, the stored snippet becomes that literal span (`Claim.reanchored`). This cut Robinhood's rejections from 22 to 7 without accepting anything not literally on the page. Rejected: fuzzy snippet matching, which would accept paraphrases.
+- Location, bio and page date each need their own verified evidence, or they are dropped (NULL). A rejected claim is kept in `stats_json.rejections` with its reason.
+- **Charset fix found here:** SEC filings declare ASCII but contain cp1252 bytes. Decoding them as UTF-8 put `�` in place of apostrophes, so no quote could match. `FetchResult.text_body` now tries the header charset, then UTF-8, then cp1252.
+
+## D19. Schema additions (Phase 3)
+
+- `sources.published_at` (page or filing date, when verified), `facts.is_current` (whether that source presented the title as current), and `roles.as_of` / `roles.note` (newest evidence date; why a role is not current, disputed, or low confidence). All nullable. Missing evidence stays NULL.
+- `sources` are rebuilt each run together with people and facts (D3). Only sources that back a stored fact are written.

+    current = [c for c in claims if c.status != "former"]
+    former = [c for c in claims if c.status == "former"]
+    newest_current = max((_ordinal(c.published_at) for c in current), default=-1)
+    newest_former = max((_ordinal(c.published_at) for c in former), default=-1)
+    note = ""
+    # A 'former' statement wins unless a current claim is strictly newer (undated = oldest).
+    is_current = bool(current) and (not former or newest_current > newest_former)
+    if former and current:
+        note = "sources disagree on whether this role is current"
+
+    # D16 proxy rule: a dated C-level newsroom/search claim older than the latest proxy, for a
+    # role the proxy doesn't list for this person, is not current. SEC claims are exempt.
+    # Undated claims can't be shown to be older: they stay current and are listed for review
+    # (the proxy lists only Section 16 officers, so e.g. a Chief People Officer may be absent).
+    if (
+        is_current
+        and seniority == "c_level"
+        and proxy_date is not None
+        and key not in proxy_keys
+        and not any(c.doc.source_type == "sec_filing" for c in current)
+    ):
+        if newest_current <= 0:
+            note = f"C-level title not in the {proxy_date} proxy; source is undated"
+        elif newest_current < _ordinal(proxy_date):
+            is_current = False
+            note = f"not listed in the {proxy_date} proxy, which is newer than this claim"
+
+    supporting = current if is_current else (former or claims)
+    dated = [c.published_at for c in supporting if c.published_at]
+    as_of = max(dated) if dated else None
+    confidence = role_confidence(supporting)
+    single = len({c.doc.url for c in supporting}) == 1
+    if (
+        is_current
+        and single
+        and as_of
+        and (today - date.fromisoformat(as_of)).days > STALE_AFTER_DAYS
+    ):
+        confidence = "low"
+        note = note or f"single source, last dated {as_of} (older than 18 months)"
+    return ResolvedRole(
+        supporting[0].title, function, seniority, is_current, as_of, confidence, claims, note
+    )
+
+
+def _apply_promotions(roles: list[ResolvedRole]) -> None:
+    """A person's older title is superseded by a newer, dated title in the same function
+    (VP of Operations in 2018, then COO from 2019). Founder roles are never superseded."""
+    for r in roles:
+        if not r.is_current or r.seniority == "founder":
+            continue
+        newest = max((_ordinal(c.published_at) for c in r.claims), default=0)
+        newer = [
+            o
+            for o in roles
+            if o is not r
+            and o.seniority != "founder"
+            and o.function == r.function
+            and newest
+            and min((_ordinal(c.published_at) for c in o.claims if c.published_at), default=0)
+            > newest
+        ]
+        if newer:
+            r.is_current = False
+            r.note = (
+                f"superseded by a later title: {newer[0].title} ({newer[0].as_of or 'undated'})"
+            )
+
+
+def _review_role(review: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], name: str, r: ResolvedRole) -> None:
+    if r.seniority == "founder" and r.claims[0].title_class.seniority != "founder":
+        return  # the founder half of "Co-founder & CEO": already listed under the main role
+    entry = {
+        "person": name,
+        "title": r.title,
+        "note": r.note,
+        "urls": sorted({c.doc.url for c in r.claims}),
+    }
+    if "disagree" in r.note:
+        review["conflicts"].append(entry | {"field": "is_current", "resolved": r.is_current})
+    elif "source is undated" in r.note:
+        review["c_level_not_in_proxy_undated"].append(entry)
+    elif "proxy" in r.note:
+        review["superseded_by_proxy"].append(entry)
+    elif "superseded by a later title" in r.note:
+        review["superseded_by_promotion"].append(entry)
+    elif "18 months" in r.note:
+        review["stale_single_source"].append(entry)
+
+
+def _seat_conflicts(people: list[ResolvedPerson], review: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]):
+    """Two people both current in the same C-level seat (e.g. two CTOs). Listed, not decided:
+    the older one may have left, or titles may overlap. Board chairs and 'other' are skipped."""
+    seats: dict[str, list[tuple[ResolvedPerson, ResolvedRole]]] = defaultdict(list)
+    for p in people:
+        for r in p.roles:
+            if r.is_current and r.seniority == "c_level" and r.function != "other":
+                seats[r.function].append((p, r))
+    for function, holders in sorted(seats.items()):
+        if len({p.full_name for p, _ in holders}) > 1:
+            review["seat_conflicts"].append(
+                {
+                    "function": function,
+                    "holders": [
+                        {"person": p.full_name, "title": r.title, "as_of": r.as_of}
+                        for p, r in sorted(holders, key=lambda h: h[1].as_of or "", reverse=True)
+                    ],
+                }
+            )
+
+
+def resolve_claims(
+    claims: list[Claim], today: date | None = None, company_id: int = 0
+) -> Resolution:
+    today = today or date.today()
+    proxy_claims = [c for c in claims if _is_proxy(c) and c.status != "former"]
+    proxy_date = max((c.published_at for c in proxy_claims if c.published_at), default=None)
+
+    review: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = defaultdict(list)
+    people: list[ResolvedPerson] = []
+    for cluster in cluster_claims(claims, company_id):
+        names = sorted({c.full_name for c in cluster})
+        if len({normalize_name(n) for n in names}) > 1:
+            review["merged_by_nickname_rule"].append({"names": names})
+        proxy_keys = {k for c in cluster if c in proxy_claims for k in _role_keys(c)}
+
+        by_key: dict[tuple[str, str], list[Claim]] = defaultdict(list)
+        for c in cluster:
+            for key in _role_keys(c):
+                by_key[key].append(c)
+        roles = [_resolve_role(k, cs, proxy_date, proxy_keys, today) for k, cs in by_key.items()]
+        _apply_promotions(roles)
+        roles.sort(key=lambda r: (not r.is_current, _SENIORITY_RANK[r.seniority], r.title))
+        live = [r for r in roles if r.is_current] or roles
+        confidence = max((r.confidence for r in live), key=_CONFIDENCE_RANK.__getitem__)
+        live_claims = [c for r in live for c in r.claims if c.status != "former"] or cluster
+        best = min(live_claims, key=_claim_sort_key)
+        person = ResolvedPerson(best.full_name, cluster, roles, confidence, best.doc.url)
+
+        ordered = sorted(cluster, key=_claim_sort_key)
+        located = [c for c in ordered if c.location]
+        if located:
+            person.location, person.location_claim = located[0].location, located[0]
+            values = sorted({c.location for c in located if c.location})
+            if len({v.casefold() for v in values}) > 1:
+                review["conflicts"].append(
+                    {"person": person.full_name, "field": "location", "values": values}
+                )
+        bios = [c for c in ordered if c.bio]
+        if bios:
+            person.bio, person.bio_claim = bios[0].bio, bios[0]
+
+        for r in roles:
+            _review_role(review, person.full_name, r)
+        if any(_blocked_host(c) for c in cluster):
+            review["from_blocked_host"].append(
+                {
+                    "person": person.full_name,
+                    "only_source": all(_blocked_host(c) for c in cluster),
+                    "urls": sorted({c.doc.url for c in cluster if _blocked_host(c)}),
+                }
+            )
+        people.append(person)
+
+    _seat_conflicts(people, review)
+    for i, a in enumerate(people):
+        for b in people[i + 1 :]:
+            ra = NameRecord(company_id, a.full_name, frozenset(r.function for r in a.roles))
+            rb = NameRecord(company_id, b.full_name, frozenset(r.function for r in b.roles))
+            if compare_identity(ra, rb) is Identity.POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE:
+                review["possible_duplicates"].append({"names": sorted([a.full_name, b.full_name])})
+    people.sort(key=lambda p: p.full_name)
+    return Resolution(people, dict(review))

1	# Claude Code Prompt — Company Leadership RAG Agent
2	
3	> Paste everything below the line into Claude Code, starting in **Plan Mode** (Shift+Tab twice). Work through the phases one at a time. Don't let it build everything in one pass. The reviewers are grading how you work with the agent, so each phase needs its own checkpoint.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Role & context
8	
9	You are a senior engineer helping me build a take-home for an AI engineering role. Reviewers will clone the repo and run it. They are evaluating:
10	1. Data sourcing.
11	2. Storage design.
12	3. Agent architecture.
13	4. How I collaborate with you: **especially how I validate what you produce.**
14	5. **How honest the system is about what it doesn't know.**
15	
16	The reviewer explicitly said: **a lean solution that works end to end beats a complex one.** The budget is 4–8 hours. If something would push past that, tell me and propose the simpler option. Optimize for correctness, provenance, and readability over feature count.
17	
18	## The task
19	
20	Input: a company domain or URL. Output:
21	1. **Collection pipeline**: find the company's leadership (C-level, VPs, Heads of departments) from public sources, collect public profile data, and store it with provenance.
22	2. **Chat interface**: an LLM-powered chat over the stored data that answers questions like "Who's their CTO?", "How many VPs do they have?", "Who heads marketing?", "Where is their CEO based?"
23	
24	Test companies: `https://meetcampfire.com/` (small private startup) and `https://robinhood.com/` (public company, NASDAQ: HOOD). The scope is these two only. Build generically, but tune and validate against these two.
25	
26	Hard rules:
27	- Real LLM calls only (no stubs or mocks in the runtime path).
28	- The repo must be clone-and-go.
29	- Commit the collected data for both companies.
30	- Ship an `.env.example`, never real keys.
31	
32	## Non-negotiable principles
33	
34	- **Every fact has a source.** No person, title, or location is stored without a source URL, a short evidence snippet, and a `retrieved_at` timestamp. The chat agent cites sources in its answers.
35	- **Never invent data.** If there's no evidence, the field stays NULL. The chat agent says "not found in the collected data" and, where useful, says what sources were checked. It never guesses.
36	- **Surface uncertainty.** Answers state when a fact comes from only one low-trust source, or when sources conflict.
37	- **Respect sources.** Honor robots.txt, rate-limit, set a descriptive User-Agent. **No LinkedIn scraping** (its ToS prohibits it), and the same goes for any other site whose ToS forbids scraping.
38	- **Config via env.** Keep the model name configurable (`LLM_MODEL`, default `claude-sonnet-5-5`).
39	
40	## Data sourcing (priority order)
41	
42	1. **Company's own site.** Find leadership/team/about/press pages via sitemap.xml, common paths (`/about`, `/team`, `/leadership`, `/company`), and nav links. This is the highest-trust source.
43	2. **SEC EDGAR** (public companies only; free official API; User-Agent must include a contact email). Use the latest 10-K "Executive Officers" section and/or the DEF 14A proxy. These are authoritative for C-level roles.
44	3. **One web search API** (Tavily, Brave, or Serper; pick one and justify it). Use targeted queries (`"{company}" VP`, `"{company}" "head of"`, `"{company}" CTO`) to find press releases, news, and conference bios, which is where most VPs and department heads appear.
45	
46	Each source is a small adapter with the same interface (`discover(company) -> list[RawDocument]`). Cache raw fetched pages to disk so re-running extraction never re-fetches. If a page needs JavaScript to render, tell me before adding a headless browser.
47	
48	## Storage: SQLite, relational, Postgres-compatible
49	
50	Rationale (put this in `docs/DECISIONS.md`): the target questions are structured (filter by role, count VPs, look up a location), so a relational model answers them exactly. A vector store would make counts and filters less reliable. SQLite keeps it clone-and-go, and a plain `schema.sql` stays Postgres-compatible.
51	
52	```
53	companies       (id, name, domain, is_public, ticker)
54	people          (id, company_id, full_name, location, bio, profile_url, confidence, updated_at)
55	roles           (id, person_id, title_raw, function, seniority, is_current)
56	                -- function: engineering|product|finance|marketing|sales|operations|legal|people|security|design|data|other
57	                -- seniority: c_level|vp|head|founder
58	sources         (id, company_id, url, source_type, fetched_at, raw_path)
59	                -- source_type: company_site|sec_filing|search
60	facts           (id, person_id, field, value, source_id, evidence_snippet, extracted_at)
61	                -- every claim + its evidence = the audit trail
62	collection_runs (id, company_id, started_at, finished_at, stats_json)
63	```
64	
65	- `people` and `roles` hold the **resolved current view**, and `facts` holds **every claim with evidence**, so conflicts are visible.
66	- `confidence` is computed deterministically from the source mix (e.g. company site or SEC filing = high, multiple search hits = medium, single search hit = low), not from the LLM's opinion.
67	- Commit `data/<domain>/leadership.db` plus a readable `data/<domain>/leadership.json` export.
68	
69	## Agent architecture: as few LLM steps as possible
70	
71	**Collection pipeline** (deterministic orchestration):
72	1. **Discover**: run the source adapters and cache raw docs. No LLM.
73	2. **Extract** (LLM, structured output via tool use + Pydantic): for each relevant chunk, return `{full_name, title_raw, function, seniority, location?, bio?, evidence_snippet}`. Return an empty list rather than guess, and leave out non-leadership roles. Before the LLM call, pre-filter chunks with keyword/heading heuristics to control cost.
74	3. **Validate & resolve** (no LLM):
75	   - Reject any extraction whose `evidence_snippet` doesn't literally appear in the source text. This catches hallucinations cheaply.
76	   - Apply deterministic title rules (CEO/CFO/VP/Head of) that override the LLM's classification on unambiguous titles.
77	   - Dedupe people by normalized name. Settle conflicts by source priority (company_site > sec_filing > search), then recency.
78	   - Write `facts`, then resolve into `people`/`roles`.
79	
80	**Chat agent**: tool-calling over typed tools, not free-form text-to-SQL.
81	- Tools: `list_leaders(company, function?, seniority?)`, `count_leaders(company, function?, seniority?)`, `get_person(company, name)` (returns facts + sources).
82	- The system prompt requires:
83	  - Answer only from tool results.
84	  - Cite source URLs.
85	  - State low confidence or conflicts.
86	  - Say "not found" when the data isn't there.
87	  - Ask which company when it's ambiguous.
88	- Keep conversation history so follow-ups work ("where is *she* based?").
89	
90	## Interface
91	
92	**Primary interface: a polished Streamlit app** (`uv run leadership ui`). It should look like an internal tool, not a demo.
93	- **Sidebar:** company selector, plus last-run stats (date, sources used, people found, LLM cost).
94	- **Chat tab:**
95	  - Answers stream in.
96	  - Each answer has a collapsible **Sources** section (links + evidence snippets) and a collapsible **Agent steps** section (tools called and with what arguments).
97	  - An empty chat shows 4–5 suggested-question buttons.
98	- **Leadership tab:** a filterable table (name, title, function, seniority, location, confidence, source count), grouped C-level / VP / Head. Low-confidence rows are visibly flagged.
99	- **Look and errors:** a clean theme in `.streamlit/config.toml` (neutral palette, one accent color). Friendly messages for a missing API key or an LLM failure, and never a raw stack trace.
100	
101	**CLI** (Typer + Rich): `leadership collect <url>`, `leadership chat <domain>`, `leadership eval <domain>`, `leadership ui`. Collection runs from the CLI, not from the UI.
102	
103	**Runs in VS Code on Windows, macOS, and Linux/WSL:**
104	- `uv` for env + deps, and every command runs as `uv run ...`. **No Makefile**, because Windows doesn't have `make` by default.
105	- VS Code files:
106	  - `.vscode/extensions.json`: Python, Pylance, Ruff.
107	  - `.vscode/settings.json`: `.venv` interpreter, Ruff format-on-save, pytest enabled.
108	  - `.vscode/launch.json`: **Launch UI**, **Collect robinhood.com**, **Collect meetcampfire.com**, **Chat CLI**, **Debug tests**.
109	- `.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf`. Use `pathlib` for paths and explicit UTF-8 for all file I/O.
110	- Load `.env` automatically. If a key is missing, print exactly which one and where to get it.
111	- **Fresh-clone test:** clone → `uv sync` → copy `.env.example` → F5 **Launch UI** must work against the committed data with only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set.
112	
113	Dependencies: Python 3.12, `httpx`, `trafilatura` (or `selectolax`), `pydantic`, `anthropic`, `streamlit`, `typer`, `rich`, `python-dotenv`. Justify anything else.
114	
115	```
116	src/leadership/
117	  sources/    company_site.py  sec_edgar.py  search.py
118	  pipeline/   discover.py  extract.py  resolve.py
119	  storage/    schema.sql  db.py  repository.py
120	  chat/       agent.py  tools.py  prompts.py
121	  ui/         app.py
122	  cli.py
123	data/meetcampfire.com/  data/robinhood.com/
124	eval/questions.yaml
125	tests/
126	docs/DECISIONS.md  docs/VALIDATION.md  docs/initial-prompt.md
127	docs/validation/  # subagent reports: <domain>-verifier.md, <domain>-scout.md
128	.claude/agents/   # project subagents (already present, don't modify)
129	session/          # Claude Code session export
130	README.md  .env.example  .gitattributes  pyproject.toml  .vscode/  .streamlit/
131	```
132	
133	## Validation (a main grading criterion, so treat it as a feature)
134	
135	- **`docs/VALIDATION.md`**: after collection, generate a checklist for each company: every person, title, location, and source URL, with a blank "Verified by Daniel: ✅ / ❌ / note" column. I'll hand-check each row against its source. Then record the errors I found, what caused each one, and what we changed to fix it. Also record **known misses**: leaders I found manually that the pipeline didn't.
136	- **`eval/questions.yaml`**: 8–10 Q&A per company, with answers I've verified by hand. Include:
137	  - the four example questions,
138	  - at least two questions the data **can't** answer, where the correct answer is "not found",
139	  - one follow-up question,
140	  - one question where sources conflict or confidence is low.
141	- `leadership eval` runs them through the real agent and prints pass/fail.
142	- **Unit tests** (offline, no keys): title rules, the evidence-snippet check, dedupe/resolve, and repository queries.
143	- Log token usage and cost per run in `collection_runs.stats_json`.
144	
145	## README must include
146	
147	- Quickstart: VS Code (F5) and terminal.
148	- Screenshots of both UI tabs.

# Claude Code Prompt — Company Leadership RAG Agent

> Paste everything below the line into Claude Code, starting in **Plan Mode** (Shift+Tab twice). Work through the phases one at a time. Don't let it build everything in one pass. The reviewers are grading how you work with the agent, so each phase needs its own checkpoint.

---

## Role & context

You are a senior engineer helping me build a take-home for an AI engineering role. Reviewers will clone the repo and run it. They are evaluating:
1. Data sourcing.
2. Storage design.
3. Agent architecture.
4. How I collaborate with you: **especially how I validate what you produce.**
5. **How honest the system is about what it doesn't know.**

The reviewer explicitly said: **a lean solution that works end to end beats a complex one.** The budget is 4–8 hours. If something would push past that, tell me and propose the simpler option. Optimize for correctness, provenance, and readability over feature count.

## The task

Input: a company domain or URL. Output:
1. **Collection pipeline**: find the company's leadership (C-level, VPs, Heads of departments) from public sources, collect public profile data, and store it with provenance.
2. **Chat interface**: an LLM-powered chat over the stored data that answers questions like "Who's their CTO?", "How many VPs do they have?", "Who heads marketing?", "Where is their CEO based?"

Test companies: `https://meetcampfire.com/` (small private startup) and `https://robinhood.com/` (public company, NASDAQ: HOOD). The scope is these two only. Build generically, but tune and validate against these two.

Hard rules:
- Real LLM calls only (no stubs or mocks in the runtime path).
- The repo must be clone-and-go.
- Commit the collected data for both companies.
- Ship an `.env.example`, never real keys.

## Non-negotiable principles

- **Every fact has a source.** No person, title, or location is stored without a source URL, a short evidence snippet, and a `retrieved_at` timestamp. The chat agent cites sources in its answers.
- **Never invent data.** If there's no evidence, the field stays NULL. The chat agent says "not found in the collected data" and, where useful, says what sources were checked. It never guesses.
- **Surface uncertainty.** Answers state when a fact comes from only one low-trust source, or when sources conflict.
- **Respect sources.** Honor robots.txt, rate-limit, set a descriptive User-Agent. **No LinkedIn scraping** (its ToS prohibits it), and the same goes for any other site whose ToS forbids scraping.
- **Config via env.** Keep the model name configurable (`LLM_MODEL`, default `claude-sonnet-5-5`).

## Data sourcing (priority order)

1. **Company's own site.** Find leadership/team/about/press pages via sitemap.xml, common paths (`/about`, `/team`, `/leadership`, `/company`), and nav links. This is the highest-trust source.
2. **SEC EDGAR** (public companies only; free official API; User-Agent must include a contact email). Use the latest 10-K "Executive Officers" section and/or the DEF 14A proxy. These are authoritative for C-level roles.
3. **One web search API** (Tavily, Brave, or Serper; pick one and justify it). Use targeted queries (`"{company}" VP`, `"{company}" "head of"`, `"{company}" CTO`) to find press releases, news, and conference bios, which is where most VPs and department heads appear.

Each source is a small adapter with the same interface (`discover(company) -> list[RawDocument]`). Cache raw fetched pages to disk so re-running extraction never re-fetches. If a page needs JavaScript to render, tell me before adding a headless browser.

## Storage: SQLite, relational, Postgres-compatible

Rationale (put this in `docs/DECISIONS.md`): the target questions are structured (filter by role, count VPs, look up a location), so a relational model answers them exactly. A vector store would make counts and filters less reliable. SQLite keeps it clone-and-go, and a plain `schema.sql` stays Postgres-compatible.

```
companies       (id, name, domain, is_public, ticker)
people          (id, company_id, full_name, location, bio, profile_url, confidence, updated_at)
roles           (id, person_id, title_raw, function, seniority, is_current)
                -- function: engineering|product|finance|marketing|sales|operations|legal|people|security|design|data|other
                -- seniority: c_level|vp|head|founder
sources         (id, company_id, url, source_type, fetched_at, raw_path)
                -- source_type: company_site|sec_filing|search
facts           (id, person_id, field, value, source_id, evidence_snippet, extracted_at)
                -- every claim + its evidence = the audit trail
collection_runs (id, company_id, started_at, finished_at, stats_json)
```

- `people` and `roles` hold the **resolved current view**, and `facts` holds **every claim with evidence**, so conflicts are visible.
- `confidence` is computed deterministically from the source mix (e.g. company site or SEC filing = high, multiple search hits = medium, single search hit = low), not from the LLM's opinion.
- Commit `data/<domain>/leadership.db` plus a readable `data/<domain>/leadership.json` export.

## Agent architecture: as few LLM steps as possible

**Collection pipeline** (deterministic orchestration):
1. **Discover**: run the source adapters and cache raw docs. No LLM.
2. **Extract** (LLM, structured output via tool use + Pydantic): for each relevant chunk, return `{full_name, title_raw, function, seniority, location?, bio?, evidence_snippet}`. Return an empty list rather than guess, and leave out non-leadership roles. Before the LLM call, pre-filter chunks with keyword/heading heuristics to control cost.
3. **Validate & resolve** (no LLM):
   - Reject any extraction whose `evidence_snippet` doesn't literally appear in the source text. This catches hallucinations cheaply.
   - Apply deterministic title rules (CEO/CFO/VP/Head of) that override the LLM's classification on unambiguous titles.
   - Dedupe people by normalized name. Settle conflicts by source priority (company_site > sec_filing > search), then recency.
   - Write `facts`, then resolve into `people`/`roles`.

**Chat agent**: tool-calling over typed tools, not free-form text-to-SQL.
- Tools: `list_leaders(company, function?, seniority?)`, `count_leaders(company, function?, seniority?)`, `get_person(company, name)` (returns facts + sources).
- The system prompt requires:
  - Answer only from tool results.
  - Cite source URLs.
  - State low confidence or conflicts.
  - Say "not found" when the data isn't there.
  - Ask which company when it's ambiguous.
- Keep conversation history so follow-ups work ("where is *she* based?").

## Interface

**Primary interface: a polished Streamlit app** (`uv run leadership ui`). It should look like an internal tool, not a demo.
- **Sidebar:** company selector, plus last-run stats (date, sources used, people found, LLM cost).
- **Chat tab:**
  - Answers stream in.
  - Each answer has a collapsible **Sources** section (links + evidence snippets) and a collapsible **Agent steps** section (tools called and with what arguments).
  - An empty chat shows 4–5 suggested-question buttons.
- **Leadership tab:** a filterable table (name, title, function, seniority, location, confidence, source count), grouped C-level / VP / Head. Low-confidence rows are visibly flagged.
- **Look and errors:** a clean theme in `.streamlit/config.toml` (neutral palette, one accent color). Friendly messages for a missing API key or an LLM failure, and never a raw stack trace.

**CLI** (Typer + Rich): `leadership collect <url>`, `leadership chat <domain>`, `leadership eval <domain>`, `leadership ui`. Collection runs from the CLI, not from the UI.

**Runs in VS Code on Windows, macOS, and Linux/WSL:**
- `uv` for env + deps, and every command runs as `uv run ...`. **No Makefile**, because Windows doesn't have `make` by default.
- VS Code files:
  - `.vscode/extensions.json`: Python, Pylance, Ruff.
  - `.vscode/settings.json`: `.venv` interpreter, Ruff format-on-save, pytest enabled.
  - `.vscode/launch.json`: **Launch UI**, **Collect robinhood.com**, **Collect meetcampfire.com**, **Chat CLI**, **Debug tests**.
- `.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf`. Use `pathlib` for paths and explicit UTF-8 for all file I/O.
- Load `.env` automatically. If a key is missing, print exactly which one and where to get it.
- **Fresh-clone test:** clone → `uv sync` → copy `.env.example` → F5 **Launch UI** must work against the committed data with only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set.

Dependencies: Python 3.12, `httpx`, `trafilatura` (or `selectolax`), `pydantic`, `anthropic`, `streamlit`, `typer`, `rich`, `python-dotenv`. Justify anything else.

```
src/leadership/
  sources/    company_site.py  sec_edgar.py  search.py
  pipeline/   discover.py  extract.py  resolve.py
  storage/    schema.sql  db.py  repository.py
  chat/       agent.py  tools.py  prompts.py
  ui/         app.py
  cli.py
data/meetcampfire.com/  data/robinhood.com/
eval/questions.yaml
tests/
docs/DECISIONS.md  docs/VALIDATION.md  docs/initial-prompt.md
docs/validation/  # subagent reports: <domain>-verifier.md, <domain>-scout.md
.claude/agents/   # project subagents (already present, don't modify)
session/          # Claude Code session export
README.md  .env.example  .gitattributes  pyproject.toml  .vscode/  .streamlit/
```

## Validation (a main grading criterion, so treat it as a feature)

- **`docs/VALIDATION.md`**: after collection, generate a checklist for each company: every person, title, location, and source URL, with a blank "Verified by Daniel: ✅ / ❌ / note" column. I'll hand-check each row against its source. Then record the errors I found, what caused each one, and what we changed to fix it. Also record **known misses**: leaders I found manually that the pipeline didn't.
- **`eval/questions.yaml`**: 8–10 Q&A per company, with answers I've verified by hand. Include:
  - the four example questions,
  - at least two questions the data **can't** answer, where the correct answer is "not found",
  - one follow-up question,
  - one question where sources conflict or confidence is low.
- `leadership eval` runs them through the real agent and prints pass/fail.
- **Unit tests** (offline, no keys): title rules, the evidence-snippet check, dedupe/resolve, and repository queries.
- Log token usage and cost per run in `collection_runs.stats_json`.

## README must include

- Quickstart: VS Code (F5) and terminal.
- Screenshots of both UI tabs.
- A Mermaid architecture diagram.
- Storage rationale.
- Sourcing and ethics notes (LinkedIn ban).
- How I validated the output, linking `VALIDATION.md` and eval results.
- Honest known limitations and coverage gaps.
- Cost per run.
- What I'd do with more time.
- **AI tools used:** Claude Code for all development (session export in `session/`), plus Claude (claude.ai) to draft this initial prompt, saved at `docs/initial-prompt.md`.

## How we work (follow this exactly)

1. **Phase 0, plan:** Before writing code, propose the plan, schema, and open questions. Wait for my approval.
2. Then build one phase at a time:
   1. Storage + schema.
   2. Source adapters + raw cache.
   3. Extract + validate/resolve.
   4. Run on both companies. Then:
      - Run `coverage-scout` for each company (blind).
      - Run `source-verifier` for each company.
      - Diff the scout list against our data.
      - Generate `VALIDATION.md` with an "Agent verdict" column next to my blank "Verified by Daniel" column, and a "Known misses" section.
      - **Stop while I hand-check the data.**
   5. Chat agent + tools.
   6. Eval + tests.
   7. UI polish.
   8. README/docs.
3. At the end of each phase:
   - Run it and show me real output.
   - Run the `phase-reviewer` subagent on the phase's diff, and fix any BLOCK or should-fix items (re-run the reviewer until it returns PASS).
   - List what you're unsure about, then stop for my review. Make small, focused commits with clear messages.
4. Record each non-trivial decision and the rejected alternative in `docs/DECISIONS.md`. The first entry is the LinkedIn ban: we rejected LinkedIn as a source because its ToS prohibits scraping, and we accept the resulting gaps in VP/department-head coverage.
5. If a source is blocked or empty, or a result looks wrong, tell me. Don't paper over it.
6. Before I submit, run `fresh-clone-tester`. Fix everything it reports under Critical and README gaps, then run it again until it returns READY TO SUBMIT.

## Subagents (in `.claude/agents/`)

| Agent | When | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `phase-reviewer` | End of every phase | Read-only code review against these rules, with a PASS / PASS WITH FIXES / BLOCK verdict |
| `coverage-scout` | Phase 4 | Blind, independent web research on each company's leadership. Measures what the pipeline missed. **Never give it our data.** |
| `source-verifier` | Phase 4, after collection | Checks every stored fact against its cached and live source and assigns a verdict per record |
| `fresh-clone-tester` | Before submission | Clones the committed repo into a temp folder, follows the README literally, and runs tests, eval, and a UI health check |

Rules for using them:
- Subagent reports are **inputs to my review, not approvals**. Summarize each one for me, and never act on a subagent's findings by changing data without telling me.
- Don't create additional subagents, and don't use subagents to write production code.
- Mention the subagent workflow in the README's "How I validated" section.

--- a/docs/DECISIONS.md
+++ b/docs/DECISIONS.md
@@ -111,3 +111,36 @@ Each entry: what we chose, what we rejected, and why. Newest at the bottom.
 ## D15. Company-site crawl limit is per run
 
 - `--max-pages` (default 60) sets how many top-ranked company-site URLs are fetched. Campfire is collected with `--max-pages 120`: its leaders appear mostly in blog bylines, and the default left 35 posts unfetched. With 120 it fetched 86 pages and hit no cap. Robinhood keeps 60: more newsroom pages there mostly add stale appointment posts and LLM cost.
+
+## D16. Currency and confidence rules (Phase 3; proxy and 18-month rules decided by Daniel)
+
+All deterministic, in `pipeline/resolve.py`. The LLM only reports what a page says (`status`: current / former / incoming / unclear).
+- **One role per (seniority, function) per person.** The best claim names it: source priority (company_site > sec_filing > search), then newest date.
+- **Former wins** unless a current claim for that role is strictly newer (undated counts as oldest). A "former" next to the title in the snippet overrides the model's status. Test: Jason Warnick ("former Chief Financial Officer" in the 2026 proxy) is never current, with or without the 2021 newsroom post.
+- **Proxy rule:** for C-level roles, a **dated** newsroom or search claim older than the latest DEF 14A, for a role the proxy doesn't list for that person, is `is_current = false`. SEC claims are exempt. **Undated** claims (e.g. the investors.robinhood.com leadership page) can't be shown to be older: they stay current and are listed in `c_level_not_in_proxy_undated`. The proxy lists only Section 16 officers, so a Chief People Officer or CISO is normally absent from it. (The first run applied the rule to undated claims too and wrongly retired 7 people. Fixed and tested.)
+- **Promotion rule:** an older title is superseded by a later dated title in the same function (Gretchen Howard: VP of Operations in 2018, then COO in 2019). Founder roles are never superseded.
+- **Confidence per role:** `high` = an SEC filing, or 2+ sources including the company site. `medium` = the company site, or 2+ sources. `low` = a single search result. **An uncorroborated single-source role last dated more than 18 months ago is `low`** and listed (`stale_single_source`). A person's confidence is that of their best current role.
+- **Listed for review, not decided:** two current holders of the same C-level seat (`seat_conflicts`, e.g. Campfire's two CTOs); sources that disagree on currency (`conflicts`); different locations; nickname merges; possible duplicates; records from bot-blocked hosts (D13).
+- People with no current role are kept (with their facts), so "who was the CFO before?" can be answered. Lists and counts include only current roles.
+- **Rejected:** letting the LLM decide currency or confidence. It doesn't know other sources or the proxy date, and its answer isn't auditable.
+
+## D17. Extraction: structured outputs, cached, pre-filtered
+
+- **Chosen:** `messages.parse(output_format=Extraction)` (Pydantic, `effort=medium`), one call per pre-filtered document, 4 in parallel.
+- **Rejected:** tool use with a forced tool choice. `claude-sonnet-5-5` rejects forced `tool_choice` (HTTP 400). Structured outputs guarantee the schema without a fake tool. The spec's "tool use + Pydantic" intent (schema-validated output) is unchanged.
+- **Pre-filter:** keep ±3 lines around role words (chief, officer, VP, head of, founder, ...) plus date lines. For SEC filings, use the executive-officers section, else the signatures. Pages with no role word skip the LLM. About 12% of documents are skipped.
+- **Context:** the prompt names the target company and domain, and asks for the employer plus a `works_at_target_company` flag. That flag rejects customers, partners, and homonymous organizations (campfire.org, robinhood.org).
+- **Cache:** responses are cached at `data/<domain>/raw/_extractions/` (gitignored with the rest of the raw data), keyed by model, prompt version, URL and exact input. Re-resolving costs $0. `--reextract` forces new calls. `stats_json` reports both this run's cost and the cost of the cached responses.
+- **Refusals / truncation:** a response without structured output is recorded in `extraction_errors` and that document is skipped. No server-side fallback model: a refusal is unlikely on public leadership text, and a silent model switch would muddy cost and provenance.
+
+## D18. Evidence check, with literal re-anchoring
+
+- A claim is kept only if all of these hold: the name appears in the cached source text; the snippet appears literally in it (whitespace, curly quotes and dashes don't count); the snippet contains the last name and the exact title; the title passes the title rules (`titles.py`); the model says the role is held at the target company; and the name has at least two tokens.
+- **Re-anchoring:** the model often takes the title from a heading but quotes a sentence that rewords it ("Vice President, Corporate Finance & Investor Relations" vs "Vice President of Corporate Finance and Investor Relations"). When the exact name and exact title are both in the source within 200 characters, the stored snippet becomes that literal span (`Claim.reanchored`). This cut Robinhood's rejections from 22 to 7 without accepting anything not literally on the page. Rejected: fuzzy snippet matching, which would accept paraphrases.
+- Location, bio and page date each need their own verified evidence, or they are dropped (NULL). A rejected claim is kept in `stats_json.rejections` with its reason.
+- **Charset fix found here:** SEC filings declare ASCII but contain cp1252 bytes. Decoding them as UTF-8 put `�` in place of apostrophes, so no quote could match. `FetchResult.text_body` now tries the header charset, then UTF-8, then cp1252.
+
+## D19. Schema additions (Phase 3)
+
+- `sources.published_at` (page or filing date, when verified), `facts.is_current` (whether that source presented the title as current), and `roles.as_of` / `roles.note` (newest evidence date; why a role is not current, disputed, or low confidence). All nullable. Missing evidence stays NULL.
+- `sources` are rebuilt each run together with people and facts (D3). Only sources that back a stored fact are written.

 """Deterministic resolution of extracted people (no LLM).
 
-This module currently holds the identity rule: deciding whether two name records for the
-same company are the same person. Phase 3 adds fact writing and conflict resolution here.
+- Identity: which claims are the same person (narrow rule, D6).
+- Roles: one role per (seniority, function) per person; the best source names it.
+- Currency: 'former' claims, and the proxy rule (D16): for C-level roles, the latest DEF 14A
+  beats older newsroom/search claims that it doesn't confirm.
+- Confidence: from source types, corroboration and age (D16).
+- Review lists for VALIDATION.md: merges, possible duplicates, conflicts, stale roles.
 """
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
+from collections import defaultdict
 from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from datetime import date
 from difflib import SequenceMatcher
 from enum import StrEnum
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
 
-from leadership.models import normalize_name
+from leadership.models import SOURCE_PRIORITY, normalize_name
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from leadership.pipeline.validate import Claim
 
 # Small, explicit nickname map. Keys and values are normalized (lowercase, no accents).
 # Prefix pairs ("vlad"/"vladimir", "dan"/"daniel") don't need an entry; see _first_names_match.
@@ -109,3 +119,283 @@ def compare_identity(a: NameRecord, b: NameRecord) -> Identity:
     if ratio >= _POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE_RATIO:
         return Identity.POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE
     return Identity.DIFFERENT
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- resolution
+
+STALE_AFTER_DAYS = 548  # 18 months
+PROXY_FORM = "DEF 14A"
+_CONFIDENCE_RANK = {"low": 0, "medium": 1, "high": 2}
+_SENIORITY_RANK = {"c_level": 0, "founder": 1, "vp": 2, "head": 3}
+
+
+def _ordinal(iso: str | None) -> int:
+    return date.fromisoformat(iso).toordinal() if iso else 0
+
+
+def _claim_sort_key(c: Claim) -> tuple:
+    """Best evidence first: source priority, then newest dated, then URL for stability."""
+    return (SOURCE_PRIORITY[c.doc.source_type], -_ordinal(c.published_at), c.doc.url, c.title)
+
+
+def _is_proxy(c: Claim) -> bool:
+    return c.doc.source_type == "sec_filing" and c.doc.meta.get("form") == PROXY_FORM
+
+
+def _blocked_host(c: Claim) -> bool:
+    return str(c.doc.meta.get("direct_fetch", "")).startswith("blocked")
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ResolvedRole:
+    title: str
+    function: str
+    seniority: str
+    is_current: bool
+    as_of: str | None
+    confidence: str
+    claims: list[Claim]
+    note: str = ""
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ResolvedPerson:
+    full_name: str
+    claims: list[Claim]
+    roles: list[ResolvedRole]
+    confidence: str
+    profile_url: str | None = None
+    location: str | None = None
+    location_claim: Claim | None = None
+    bio: str | None = None
+    bio_claim: Claim | None = None
+
+    @property
+    def is_current(self) -> bool:
+        return any(r.is_current for r in self.roles)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Resolution:
+    people: list[ResolvedPerson]
+    review: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]
+
+
+def cluster_claims(claims: list[Claim], company_id: int = 0) -> list[list[Claim]]:
+    """Group claims into people with compare_identity (SAME only), best evidence first."""
+    clusters: list[list[Claim]] = []
+    for claim in sorted(claims, key=_claim_sort_key):
+        rec = NameRecord(company_id, claim.full_name, frozenset({claim.title_class.function}))
+        for cluster in clusters:
+            functions = frozenset(c.title_class.function for c in cluster)
+            if compare_identity(rec, NameRecord(company_id, cluster[0].full_name, functions)) is (
+                Identity.SAME
+            ):
+                cluster.append(claim)
+                break
+        else:
+            clusters.append([claim])
+    return clusters
+
+
+def _role_keys(c: Claim) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
+    keys = [(c.title_class.seniority, c.title_class.function)]
+    if c.title_class.also_founder:
+        keys.append(("founder", "other"))
+    return keys
+
+
+def role_confidence(claims: list[Claim]) -> str:
+    """high: an SEC filing, or 2+ sources incl. the company site. medium: the company site,
+    or 2+ sources. low: a single search result."""
+    urls = {c.doc.url for c in claims}
+    types = {c.doc.source_type for c in claims}
+    if "sec_filing" in types or (len(urls) >= 2 and "company_site" in types):
+        return "high"
+    if "company_site" in types or len(urls) >= 2:
+        return "medium"
+    return "low"
+
+
+def _resolve_role(
+    key: tuple[str, str],
+    claims: list[Claim],
+    proxy_date: str | None,
+    proxy_keys: set[tuple[str, str]],
+    today: date,
+) -> ResolvedRole:
+    seniority, function = key
+    claims = sorted(claims, key=_claim_sort_key)
+    current = [c for c in claims if c.status != "former"]
+    former = [c for c in claims if c.status == "former"]
+    newest_current = max((_ordinal(c.published_at) for c in current), default=-1)
+    newest_former = max((_ordinal(c.published_at) for c in former), default=-1)
+    note = ""
+    # A 'former' statement wins unless a current claim is strictly newer (undated = oldest).
+    is_current = bool(current) and (not former or newest_current > newest_former)
+    if former and current:
+        note = "sources disagree on whether this role is current"
+
+    # D16 proxy rule: a dated C-level newsroom/search claim older than the latest proxy, for a
+    # role the proxy doesn't list for this person, is not current. SEC claims are exempt.
+    # Undated claims can't be shown to be older: they stay current and are listed for review
+    # (the proxy lists only Section 16 officers, so e.g. a Chief People Officer may be absent).
+    if (
+        is_current
+        and seniority == "c_level"
+        and proxy_date is not None
+        and key not in proxy_keys
+        and not any(c.doc.source_type == "sec_filing" for c in current)
+    ):
+        if newest_current <= 0:
+            note = f"C-level title not in the {proxy_date} proxy; source is undated"
+        elif newest_current < _ordinal(proxy_date):
+            is_current = False
+            note = f"not listed in the {proxy_date} proxy, which is newer than this claim"
+
+    supporting = current if is_current else (former or claims)
+    dated = [c.published_at for c in supporting if c.published_at]
+    as_of = max(dated) if dated else None
+    confidence = role_confidence(supporting)
+    single = len({c.doc.url for c in supporting}) == 1
+    if (
+        is_current
+        and single
+        and as_of
+        and (today - date.fromisoformat(as_of)).days > STALE_AFTER_DAYS
+    ):
+        confidence = "low"
+        note = note or f"single source, last dated {as_of} (older than 18 months)"
+    return ResolvedRole(
+        supporting[0].title, function, seniority, is_current, as_of, confidence, claims, note
+    )
+
+
+def _apply_promotions(roles: list[ResolvedRole]) -> None:
+    """A person's older title is superseded by a newer, dated title in the same function
+    (VP of Operations in 2018, then COO from 2019). Founder roles are never superseded."""
+    for r in roles:
+        if not r.is_current or r.seniority == "founder":
+            continue
+        newest = max((_ordinal(c.published_at) for c in r.claims), default=0)
+        newer = [
+            o
+            for o in roles
+            if o is not r
+            and o.seniority != "founder"
+            and o.function == r.function
+            and newest
+            and min((_ordinal(c.published_at) for c in o.claims if c.published_at), default=0)
+            > newest
+        ]
+        if newer:
+            r.is_current = False
+            r.note = (
+                f"superseded by a later title: {newer[0].title} ({newer[0].as_of or 'undated'})"
+            )
+
+
+def _review_role(review: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], name: str, r: ResolvedRole) -> None:
+    if r.seniority == "founder" and r.claims[0].title_class.seniority != "founder":
+        return  # the founder half of "Co-founder & CEO": already listed under the main role
+    entry = {
+        "person": name,
+        "title": r.title,
+        "note": r.note,
+        "urls": sorted({c.doc.url for c in r.claims}),
+    }
+    if "disagree" in r.note:
+        review["conflicts"].append(entry | {"field": "is_current", "resolved": r.is_current})
+    elif "source is undated" in r.note:
+        review["c_level_not_in_proxy_undated"].append(entry)
+    elif "proxy" in r.note:
+        review["superseded_by_proxy"].append(entry)
+    elif "superseded by a later title" in r.note:
+        review["superseded_by_promotion"].append(entry)
+    elif "18 months" in r.note:
+        review["stale_single_source"].append(entry)
+
+
+def _seat_conflicts(people: list[ResolvedPerson], review: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]):
+    """Two people both current in the same C-level seat (e.g. two CTOs). Listed, not decided:
+    the older one may have left, or titles may overlap. Board chairs and 'other' are skipped."""
+    seats: dict[str, list[tuple[ResolvedPerson, ResolvedRole]]] = defaultdict(list)
+    for p in people:
+        for r in p.roles:
+            if r.is_current and r.seniority == "c_level" and r.function != "other":
+                seats[r.function].append((p, r))
+    for function, holders in sorted(seats.items()):
+        if len({p.full_name for p, _ in holders}) > 1:
+            review["seat_conflicts"].append(
+                {
+                    "function": function,
+                    "holders": [
+                        {"person": p.full_name, "title": r.title, "as_of": r.as_of}
+                        for p, r in sorted(holders, key=lambda h: h[1].as_of or "", reverse=True)
+                    ],
+                }
+            )
+
+
+def resolve_claims(
+    claims: list[Claim], today: date | None = None, company_id: int = 0
+) -> Resolution:
+    today = today or date.today()
+    proxy_claims = [c for c in claims if _is_proxy(c) and c.status != "former"]
+    proxy_date = max((c.published_at for c in proxy_claims if c.published_at), default=None)
+
+    review: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = defaultdict(list)
+    people: list[ResolvedPerson] = []
+    for cluster in cluster_claims(claims, company_id):
+        names = sorted({c.full_name for c in cluster})
+        if len({normalize_name(n) for n in names}) > 1:
+            review["merged_by_nickname_rule"].append({"names": names})
+        proxy_keys = {k for c in cluster if c in proxy_claims for k in _role_keys(c)}
+
+        by_key: dict[tuple[str, str], list[Claim]] = defaultdict(list)
+        for c in cluster:
+            for key in _role_keys(c):
+                by_key[key].append(c)
+        roles = [_resolve_role(k, cs, proxy_date, proxy_keys, today) for k, cs in by_key.items()]
+        _apply_promotions(roles)
+        roles.sort(key=lambda r: (not r.is_current, _SENIORITY_RANK[r.seniority], r.title))
+        live = [r for r in roles if r.is_current] or roles
+        confidence = max((r.confidence for r in live), key=_CONFIDENCE_RANK.__getitem__)
+        live_claims = [c for r in live for c in r.claims if c.status != "former"] or cluster
+        best = min(live_claims, key=_claim_sort_key)
+        person = ResolvedPerson(best.full_name, cluster, roles, confidence, best.doc.url)
+
+        ordered = sorted(cluster, key=_claim_sort_key)
+        located = [c for c in ordered if c.location]
+        if located:
+            person.location, person.location_claim = located[0].location, located[0]
+            values = sorted({c.location for c in located if c.location})
+            if len({v.casefold() for v in values}) > 1:
+                review["conflicts"].append(
+                    {"person": person.full_name, "field": "location", "values": values}
+                )
+        bios = [c for c in ordered if c.bio]
+        if bios:
+            person.bio, person.bio_claim = bios[0].bio, bios[0]
+
+        for r in roles:
+            _review_role(review, person.full_name, r)
+        if any(_blocked_host(c) for c in cluster):
+            review["from_blocked_host"].append(
+                {
+                    "person": person.full_name,
+                    "only_source": all(_blocked_host(c) for c in cluster),
+                    "urls": sorted({c.doc.url for c in cluster if _blocked_host(c)}),
+                }
+            )
+        people.append(person)
+
+    _seat_conflicts(people, review)
+    for i, a in enumerate(people):
+        for b in people[i + 1 :]:
+            ra = NameRecord(company_id, a.full_name, frozenset(r.function for r in a.roles))
+            rb = NameRecord(company_id, b.full_name, frozenset(r.function for r in b.roles))
+            if compare_identity(ra, rb) is Identity.POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE:
+                review["possible_duplicates"].append({"names": sorted([a.full_name, b.full_name])})
+    people.sort(key=lambda p: p.full_name)
+    return Resolution(people, dict(review))

1	"""LLM extraction: one structured-output call per pre-filtered document.
2	
3	The model only *reads*: it returns people with verbatim evidence. Everything that decides what
4	is stored (evidence check, title rules, dedupe, currency, confidence) is deterministic code in
5	validate.py and resolve.py. Responses are cached on disk (keyed by model, prompt version and
6	the exact input), so re-running resolution costs nothing; `--reextract` ignores the cache.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import hashlib
12	import json
13	import logging
14	from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
15	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
16	from pathlib import Path
17	from typing import Literal
18	
19	import anthropic
20	from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
21	
22	from leadership.config import require_setting
23	from leadership.sources.base import Company, RawDocument
24	
25	log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
26	
27	PROMPT_VERSION = "1"
28	MAX_TOKENS = 16_000
29	EFFORT = "medium"
30	WORKERS = 4
31	# USD per million tokens (input, output). Unknown models are still run; cost is reported null.
32	PRICES = {
33	    "claude-sonnet-5-5": (2.00, 10.00),
34	    "claude-sonnet-5": (2.00, 10.00),
35	    "claude-opus-5-5": (4.00, 20.00),
36	    "claude-haiku-5-5": (0.10, 0.50),
37	}
38	
39	
40	class ExtractedPerson(BaseModel):
41	    full_name: str = Field(description="The person's name exactly as written on the page.")
42	    title: str = Field(
43	        description="Their job title copied verbatim from the evidence snippet, without the "
44	        "company name. Example: 'Chief Financial Officer', 'VP, Engineering', 'Head of Product'."
45	    )
46	    employer: str = Field(description="Organization this title is held at, as the page says it.")
47	    works_at_target_company: bool = Field(
48	        description="True only if the title is held at the target company (not a customer, "
49	        "investor, partner, previous employer, or a different organization with a similar name)."
50	    )
51	    status: Literal["current", "former", "incoming", "unclear"] = Field(
52	        description="'former' if the page says they left, were replaced, or uses 'former'/'ex-'/"
53	        "'previously'; 'incoming' if announced but not started; 'current' only if the page "
54	        "presents the title as held now (as of the page date)."
55	    )
56	    evidence_snippet: str = Field(
57	        description="A verbatim quote from the page (one or two sentences, under 300 "
58	        "characters) that contains both the person's name and the title."
59	    )
60	    location: str | None = Field(
61	        description="City/region where the person is based, only if the page states it; else null."
62	    )
63	    location_snippet: str | None = Field(
64	        description="Verbatim quote stating the location; null when location is null."
65	    )
66	    bio: str | None = Field(
67	        description="One verbatim sentence from the page describing their background; else null."
68	    )
69	
70	
71	class Extraction(BaseModel):
72	    page_published_date: str | None = Field(
73	        description="Publication date shown on the page, as YYYY-MM-DD; null if none is shown."
74	    )
75	    published_date_snippet: str | None = Field(
76	        description="The verbatim text on the page that shows that date; null if none."
77	    )
78	    people: list[ExtractedPerson]
79	
80	
81	SYSTEM = """You extract company leadership from one web page or filing. You read; you never guess.
82	
83	Rules:
84	- Target company: {name} (website {domain}). Only include people whose title is held AT the
85	  target company. Exclude people at other organizations that share the name, customers,
86	  investors, partners, authors of quoted studies, and people from other companies mentioned in
87	  the text.
88	- In scope: C-level officers (Chief ... Officer, CEO, CFO, President, General Counsel),
89	  founders, Vice Presidents (VP, SVP, EVP), and Heads of a function (Head of X). Skip board-
90	  only directors, managers, engineers, and other staff.
91	- Every value must be copied verbatim from the page text: name, title, snippet, location, bio,
92	  date. Do not translate, expand abbreviations, or fix typos. If something is not stated, use
93	  null.
94	- The evidence_snippet must contain both the name and the title, exactly as they appear.
95	- Mark status 'former' whenever the page says the person left, was replaced, or held the role
96	  in the past ("former CFO", "previously VP"). A page that announces an appointment presents it
97	  as current as of the page date.
98	- If the page lists no in-scope people at the target company, return an empty list.
99	- Text marked [...] was removed by a filter; only use what you see."""
100	
101	
102	@dataclass
103	class ExtractResult:
104	    doc: RawDocument
105	    extraction: Extraction | None
106	    input_tokens: int = 0
107	    output_tokens: int = 0
108	    from_cache: bool = False
109	    error: str = ""
110	
111	
112	@dataclass
113	class ExtractStats:
114	    llm_calls: int = 0
115	    cached: int = 0
116	    input_tokens: int = 0  # this run's API calls only
117	    output_tokens: int = 0
118	    cached_input_tokens: int = 0  # what the cached responses cost when they were made
119	    cached_output_tokens: int = 0
120	    errors: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
121	
122	    def cost_usd(self, model: str, include_cached: bool = False) -> float | None:
123	        price = PRICES.get(model)
124	        if price is None:
125	            return None
126	        tin, tout = self.input_tokens, self.output_tokens
127	        if include_cached:
128	            tin, tout = tin + self.cached_input_tokens, tout + self.cached_output_tokens
129	        return round((tin * price[0] + tout * price[1]) / 1e6, 4)
130	
131	
132	def _user_prompt(doc: RawDocument, text: str) -> str:
133	    meta_date = doc.meta.get("published_date") or doc.meta.get("filing_date") or "unknown"
134	    return (
135	        f"Source URL: {doc.url}\nPage title: {doc.title}\n"
136	        f"Publication date from metadata (may be missing): {meta_date}\n\n"
137	        f"<page>\n{text}\n</page>"
138	    )
139	
140	
141	class Extractor:
142	    def __init__(self, company: Company, model: str, cache_dir: Path, reextract: bool = False):
143	        self.company = company
144	        self.model = model
145	        self.cache_dir = cache_dir
146	        self.reextract = reextract
147	        self.system = SYSTEM.format(name=company.name, domain=company.domain)
148	        self._client: anthropic.Anthropic | None = None
149	
150	    def _client_lazy(self) -> anthropic.Anthropic:
151	        if self._client is None:
152	            self._client = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=require_setting("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"))
153	        return self._client
154	
155	    def _cache_path(self, doc: RawDocument, text: str) -> Path:
156	        key = hashlib.sha256(
157	            "\x00".join([self.model, PROMPT_VERSION, self.system, doc.url, text]).encode("utf-8")
158	        ).hexdigest()[:24]
159	        return self.cache_dir / f"{key}.json"
160	
161	    def extract(self, doc: RawDocument, text: str) -> ExtractResult:
162	        path = self._cache_path(doc, text)
163	        if path.exists() and not self.reextract:
164	            data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
165	            usage = data.get("usage", {})
166	            return ExtractResult(
167	                doc,
168	                Extraction.model_validate(data["extraction"]),
169	                usage.get("input_tokens", 0),
170	                usage.get("output_tokens", 0),
171	                from_cache=True,
172	            )
173	        try:
174	            response = self._client_lazy().messages.parse(
175	                model=self.model,
176	                max_tokens=MAX_TOKENS,
177	                system=self.system,
178	                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": _user_prompt(doc, text)}],
179	                output_format=Extraction,
180	                output_config={"effort": EFFORT},
181	            )
182	        except anthropic.AuthenticationError as exc:
183	            raise RuntimeError("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY was rejected (HTTP 401)") from exc
184	        except anthropic.APIError as exc:
185	            log.warning("extraction failed for %s: %s", doc.url, exc)
186	            return ExtractResult(doc, None, error=f"API error: {exc}")
187	        usage = response.usage
188	        result = ExtractResult(doc, None, usage.input_tokens, usage.output_tokens)
189	        if response.stop_reason in ("refusal", "max_tokens") or response.parsed_output is None:
190	            result.error = f"no structured output (stop_reason={response.stop_reason})"
191	            return result
192	        result.extraction = response.parsed_output
193	        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
194	        payload = {
195	            "url": doc.url,
196	            "model": self.model,
197	            "prompt_version": PROMPT_VERSION,
198	            "usage": {"input_tokens": usage.input_tokens, "output_tokens": usage.output_tokens},
199	            "extraction": result.extraction.model_dump(),
200	        }
201	        path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
202	        return result
203	
204	    def extract_all(
205	        self, jobs: list[tuple[RawDocument, str]]
206	    ) -> tuple[list[ExtractResult], ExtractStats]:
207	        stats = ExtractStats()
208	        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=WORKERS) as pool:
209	            results = list(pool.map(lambda job: self.extract(*job), jobs))
210	        for r in results:
211	            if r.from_cache:
212	                stats.cached += 1
213	                stats.cached_input_tokens += r.input_tokens
214	                stats.cached_output_tokens += r.output_tokens
215	            else:
216	                stats.llm_calls += 1
217	                stats.input_tokens += r.input_tokens
218	                stats.output_tokens += r.output_tokens
219	            if r.error:
220	                stats.errors.append({"url": r.doc.url, "error": r.error})
221	        return results, stats
